# Speccify 0.10.0

Speccify 0.10.0 makes the five-resource workspace easier to install, arrange
and use every day: **Specs**, **Skills**, **UseCases**, **Rules** and **Versions**
stay together in one app with the existing settings and update channels.

## A complete runtime, ready automatically

Speccify now includes its own Python interpreter and every package needed by
its Core, CLI and MCP. The first start and later app updates prepare that
runtime automatically from the installed files. There is no separate Python
setup, Engine installation click or package download. Your existing Python,
Conda and project environments remain unchanged.

Each runtime generation is checked before activation. A failed preparation
keeps the previous generation intact; **Settings → Environment** shows progress,
errors and the repair action. Old generations remain available for running
processes and existing external MCP configurations.

## Arrange the workspace around the task

- **Screens A and B** keep two arrangements for a project. Switch from the
  toolbar or open the other screen in its own window.
- Reorder tabs, move unused tabs to the parked area and split the bottom
  workspace. Layout presets and the last confirmed arrangement help new
  projects start with a familiar workspace.
- Edit a Spec directly in its Properties inspector. Resource, tab and
  inspector context menus expose the relevant actions in place.
- Markdown toolbar menus group heading, list and code options. Rules grids
  close through the same tab controls as other documents.

## Start projects and keep questions visible

Create a project with its own `.agent` folder or clone a repository directly.
The dashboard offers focused starting actions and a Speccify-aware assistant
without requiring a project first.

The Inbox brings questions and attention notices together while keeping their
source project and terminal session distinct. Attention buttons explain what
is needed and lead to the relevant question or review. The Actions inspector
shows every open question and records answers in the canonical Spec document.

## Follow behavior and versions

Workflows support inline editing of their linked domain and UI UseCases.
UseCase timelines show changes and version assignments without exposing raw
draft and state identifiers as the main navigation.

Version Notes belong to one product version and supply its release notes.
Explicit Beta versions share the final version's family and can reach testers
through the opt-in Beta update channel. Version-bound delivery uses a separate
release branch, resumable phases and a visible journal so development can
continue independently.

## Updates and maintenance

Update blockers identify the project and unsaved document. **Save all and
install** uses the documents' normal save paths and checks every window again
before restarting. It does not discard work to force an update.

Windows verification and browser startup handling have been strengthened.
Obsolete Suite, Studio and separate Acceptance application code has been
removed; the normal Speccify installation identity is unchanged. Repository
guidance now follows this single-app scope.

## Update or install

Use **Environment → Updates** in Speccify, or install from the
[download page](https://speccify.io/download/). Resolve genuine unsaved work
before restarting. The bundled runtime is prepared automatically afterward.

Linux in-app updates apply to AppImage. Update deb/rpm installations through
the package manager. Versions 0.8.7 and earlier need a fresh installer once
because they use the former private update feed.

## Verification and limits

Development verification passed 581 desktop Rust tests, 1,380 frontend tests
and 946 Python tests. The complete runtime was built and exercised on macOS
ARM64, Windows x64, Linux x64 and Linux ARM64. Actual mouse and keyboard tests
on macOS and Windows covered automatic preparation, resource navigation and
repair while external networking was blocked. Windows tests used the x64 app
under Windows 11 ARM64 emulation and verified that its CLI loads the private
Microsoft runtime DLL.

Publication requires the full CI at the release candidate and independent
checks of update signatures, the manifest, macOS notarization and the actual
bundled runtime. The previous-version productive macOS updater transition is
recorded in the [release guide](https://speccify.io/releases/0-10-0/) after it
has been observed. Interactive installation of these final release packages
on Windows and Linux is not claimed by the development tests.

The private Python distribution increases download and disk usage. Python
security updates arrive through app updates; retained runtime generations
consume additional space. Windows Authenticode signing is not configured,
so the existing SmartScreen warning can appear. Notification delivery follows
the operating system's permissions and Focus settings.
